newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU edge down - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU edge down - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad group of countries joining Germany at the launch of European economic and monetary union in 1999 edged lower in the past week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

The likelihood of Italy being a first entrant for the European single currency fell to 73 percent from 79 last week, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator." The calculator is derived from the interest-rate swaps market.
Spanish membership chances also fell to 79 percent on Friday from 83 percent a week ago.
The probability of France and Belgium joining Germany in monetary union on schedule in 1999 was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.
Portugal, Denmark and Ireland edged higher, however, with the expected probability of each country joining EMU nudging up from last week.
Britain, viewed as the least likely country to join EMU at its start, saw its probability slip to 25 percent from 27 percent.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
